stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Pull the mass to $x_0$, release, and watch it oscillate. Sweep every slider — mass $m$, stiffness $k$, initial displacement $x_0$ — and let the system complete at least one full period.
stages.concept: Free elastic pendulum: $\ddot{x} + \dfrac{k}{m}\,x = 0$. Solution $x(t) = x_0\,\cos(\omega_0 t)$ with $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$ and period $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$. The amplitude only depends on how far you pulled it; the period only depends on $m$ and $k$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match the orange target: your live $x(t)$ curve must pass through the marker at time $t^*$ with displacement $x^*$. Tune $m$, $k$, $x_0$ so the curves overlay.
stages.concept: The marker fixes both the period AND the amplitude. $x^* = x_0\,\cos(\omega_0 t^*)$, so setting $x_0$ alone is not enough — you must also match the period $T_0^* = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ that puts the curve at $x^*$ at $t = t^*$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The live curve is hidden. Read the target's period $T_0^*$ and amplitude $x_0^*$ off the chart, set $m$, $k$, $x_0$ so that $2\pi\sqrt{m/k} = T_0^*$ and $x_0 = x_0^*$, then press RUN.
stages.concept: Two invariants to extract from the target: the period $T_0^*$ (time between two successive maxima) and the amplitude $x_0^*$ (peak displacement). Then any $(m, k)$ pair with $m/k = (T_0^*/2\pi)^2$ works.

labels.peek_hint: count peaks: T0 = time between two successive maxima; amplitude = peak value on the x-axis
labels.tip1: sweep m, k, x0 — watch how the period depends on m/k, and the amplitude on x0
labels.tip2: adjust m, k, x0 so your curve passes through the orange marker at (t*, x*)
labels.tip3: read T0* and x0* from the target curve, set m/k and x0 to match, then RUN

1.1: Move each of the three sliders in turn and watch what changes on the chart.
1.2: The period only depends on m and k. The amplitude only depends on x0. Prove this to yourself by sweeping each in isolation.
1.3: Full cycle means the curve goes from +x0 down to -x0 and back to +x0. Wait for one complete oscillation, then advance.

2.1: First compute the target period T0* that fits the marker: try x* / cos(omega * t*) = x0 for a few guesses.
2.2: Increasing m or decreasing k slows oscillation (larger T0). Increasing x0 raises the peaks without changing the timing.
2.3: The pair (m, k) is not unique — only the ratio m/k matters for the period. Any m/k = (T0*/(2·pi))^2 works.

3.1: Find two consecutive peaks on the target curve. The time between them is T0*.
3.2: Read the maximum value of the target curve — that is your amplitude x0*.
3.3: Set x0 = x0*. Then pick any (m, k) with m/k = (T0*/(2·pi))^2. Press RUN.
